contentBlocks.text: You have an opinion and reasons. Today let's put them together into an organized paragraph, with a clear beginning, middle, and end.

A strong opinion paragraph has three parts: an opening sentence (your opinion), the middle (your reasons, one at a time), and a closing sentence that wraps it up. Try this structure: 'Students should have a class pet. First, a pet teaches responsibility. Second, caring for a pet can reduce stress. For these reasons, our class should get a pet.' Notice how the closing sentence restates the opinion in a slightly new way.
Opening, reasons, closing — that's the shape of a real opinion paragraph. Tomorrow we'll learn strong linking words that make your writing flow even better.

objectives: Organize an opinion statement, supporting reasons, and a closing sentence into a structured paragraph
Write a closing sentence that restates the opinion without simply repeating the exact same words
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Read the class-pet example paragraph together, identifying the opening, reasons, and closing.
2. Discuss why a closing sentence matters, even though it 'repeats' the opinion.
3. Using this week's opinion and reasons, build a full paragraph together orally.
4. Move to the worksheet: write the full opinion paragraph using the structure.
5. Close by reading the finished paragraph aloud together.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide sentence starters for each of the three parts (opening, reason 1, reason 2, closing)
Ready for more: add a third reason to strengthen the paragraph further
For a child who enjoys reading their work aloud, have them present their paragraph like a mini persuasive speech
teacherGuide.answerKey: Open-ended writing — check for a clear opening (opinion), at least two organized reasons, and a closing sentence that returns to the opinion.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Organizing an opinion paragraph with a clear structure is a core Grade 3 opinion-writing standard (matching Common Core W.3.1a-d), the payoff for this week's opinion-and-reasons groundwork.

generationData.instructions: Write a full opinion paragraph using your opinion and reasons from this week: opening, reasons, closing.

prompts.prompt: Write your full opinion paragraph below.
